name: design-doc
description: Run an assumptions-first architecture design — registers with stable IDs (A#/DQ#/V#), decision-by-question rounds with a recorded escape hatch, a mid-process adversarial review, a library of quantitative components (request paths, load ceilings, number tables that open on the claim they make) whose estimates are gated on named spikes — and ship the result as an interactive HTML doc that opens on a full-screen summary deck of 3–5 panels (or one poster) that runs as one argument, draws its system diagram with Mermaid behind a ten-node overview in a pan-and-zoom card that stays drawn under the deck, cites every entry by a human-readable handle in parentheses, twins every register entry with a plain-English version the reader sees first, turns every path:line in the evidence into a GitHub link with a hover preview of the source behind a deployed token, carries declared interactive components (what-if, steps, timeline, matrix, and the self-laying-out compare figures flow and lanes, where each callout names the decision that fixes it) plus compiled TSX as the escape hatch, links every decision and open item to the pull requests that land it with live GitHub state, replays the interview round by round, and, behind a deployed key, answers questions from the whole document with grounded follow-ups and moves the page from an Ask bar that stays collapsed at the bottom right until it docks into an assistant panel, and from a Cmd-K palette that answers inline, plus a PDF printed from the same page, written as a humble proposal that explains and asks for feedback rather than sells.
